images.filename: Halifax crew before take-off WWII IWM D 6028.jpg
images.caption: Interior of a Handley-Page Halifax B Mk II Series I of No. 35 Squadron RAF, looking forward from the flight engineer's in-flight position, prior to take-off from Linton-on-Ouse, Yorkshire. We see here the flight engineer sitting on the fold-down "dicky" seat on the right of the pilot, which was the flight engineer's usual position on takeoff so he could assist the pilot with the throttles, which were between them. Below the flight engineer can be seen the navigator at his position with the front gunner alongside him.
images.alt: Interior of a Handley-Page Halifax B Mk II Series I of No. 35 Squadron RAF, looking forward from the flight engineer's in-flight position, prior to take-off from Linton-on-Ouse, Yorkshire. We see here the flight engineer sitting on the fold-down "dicky" seat on the right of the pilot, which was the flight engineer's usual position on takeoff so he could assist the pilot with the throttles, which were between them. images.filename: RCAF Lancaster Mk II RAF Linton-on-Ouse WWII HU 56276.jpg
images.caption: IWM caption : Avro Lancaster B Mark II, LL725 'EQ-C', of No. 408 Squadron RCAF, on the ground at Linton-on-Ouse, Yorkshire. Armourers are backing a tractor and trolley loaded with a 4,000 lb HE bomb ('Cookie') and incendiaries under the open bomb-bay. LL725 was lost over Hamburg on 28/29 July 1944.

images.caption: Royal Air Force (RAF) Percival Provost T1 registration WV562, c/n PAC/56/F/108.  Built 1954.  Flew with 22 Flying Training School (22FTS) at RAF Syerston, which was later renumbered as No. 1 Flying Training School RAF (1FTS) and moved to RAF Linton-on-Ouse.  Retired in 1959 as replaced by Jet Provosts.  Used for ground instruction at RAF Henlow and RAF Cranwell until moved to Cosford museum in 1979.  During 2014 she was temporarily painted in Sultan of Oman Air Force colours for an exhibition at Hendon.  She has now returned to Cosford and her RAF colours.  Currently on display in Hangar 1 at the RAF Museum Cosford, Shropshire, UK.  14th August 2016.
